data.name: Carmela
data.gender_notes: Carmela is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word 'carmel', meaning 'garden', 'fruitful' or 'vineyard'. The mountain of Carmel in the Bible was significant for its fruitfulness and association with God. The name Carmela symbolizes the fruitfulness of the spirit and the connection to God. The name Carmela carries the meaning “Song of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Carmela usually hope their child will grow to embody song of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of God's grace and fruitfulness in one's life.
data.etymology: Carmela belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Song of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Carmela total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: כרמלה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם כרמלה הוא עברי ומשמעותו גן אלוהים או כרמל קודש. הכרמל הוא מקום קדוש בהיסטוריה היהודית והוא מזוהה עם הנביא אליהו. השם מבטא את הקשר בין האדם לאלוהים ולטבע.

in_greek.name: Καρμέλα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Καρμέλα είναι ελληνικό και σημαίνει Κήπος του Θεού ή Κάρμηλος. Το Κάρμηλος είναι βουνό στην Παλαιστίνη που συνδέεται με τον προφήτη Ηλία. Το όνομα εκφράζει τη σχέση μεταξύ του ανθρώπου και του Θεού και της φύσης.

in_latin.name: Carmela
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Carmela est Latinum et significat Hortus Dei seu Carmelus. Carmelus est mons in Palaestina situs qui cum propheta Elia coniungitur. Nomen hoc exprimit relationem inter hominem et Deum et naturam.

in_english.name: Carmela
in_english.long_meaning: The name Carmela is of Hebrew origin, meaning 'Garden of God' or 'Orchard'. It is derived from the Hebrew word 'Kerem', which refers to a vineyard or an orchard, and 'El', meaning God. The name is associated with Mount Carmel, a sacred site in Jewish history and the location of the prophet Elijah's ministry. In Christian tradition, the name Carmela symbolizes a connection to God and nature, reflecting a spiritual and harmonious relationship.

data.cultural_impact: Carmela is a beautiful and elegant name originating from the Hebrew language of the Old Testament, adding a rich cultural background to its bearer. It has been a popular name among Christian communities across various cultures and regions.
data.spiritual_significance: Carmela is a name steeped in spiritual meaning, symbolizing the fruitfulness of the spirit and the connection to God. The mountain of Carmel in the Bible was a place where God revealed himself to the prophets Elijah and Elisha, and it was known for its fruitfulness and abundance. The name Carmela reflects the abundant blessings of the spiritual life. It serves as a reminder that just as the land of Carmel was fruitful, so too can the human spirit be when connected to God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Carmela, meaning "fruitful vineyard," symbolizes the Christian's spiritual growth and connection to God, as they bear the fruits of the Spirit in their lives. It is a reminder of the promise of eternal life in the vineyard of the Lord.

historical_references.reference: Born in southern Italy in the late 1400s, Carmela was a renowned opera singer who performed throughout Europe.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Carmela remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Ruth Carmela from Rome, Italy embodies the meaning of Carmela - "Song of God". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
